summary.value: The Slovenian Barred Hen is a laying breed begun in 1970 by animal scientists at the University of Ljubljana, who built it from Barred and White Plymouth Rocks. They selected for body size, good laying and a clean barred pattern. The feathers show crisp alternating bands of black and white, and roosters look paler than hens. Birds have a medium single comb, small red earlobes, orange eyes and light yellow legs with darker toes. It is the heaviest of the Slovenian layer breeds: roosters weigh about 6.6 to 7.7 pounds and hens about 5 to 6 pounds. Hens begin laying at around 20 weeks and produce some 240 to 250 light brown eggs a year, averaging about 59 grams. The breed is also a parent of the Prelux Black and Prelux Barred commercial layers. Slovenia counted about 1,270 birds in 2020, most of them at the university's poultry center.
